points.text: Claim that Ligeralde et al. did not use spatiotemporal retinal waves is inaccurate.
Temporal-shuffle experiment breaks contrastive learning entirely, cannot isolate spatial statistics; use reconstruction objective.
Training with backprop limits biological plausibility.
Methods lack description of the unsupervised temporal learning method.
'Self-organization' conflated with representational similarity; no topography or wiring-economy consideration.
Model RSMs not compared with human/brain data.
Missing control training on other stimuli (gratings, natural video) to isolate retinal-wave role.
Some figures such as 4(d) are low-resolution and unreadable.
Incremental: mirrors Ligeralde et al. with ViT and ViT-CoT loss substituted.
No comparison against prior models trained on retinal waves (Ligeralde, ReWaRD).
Training 100 epochs biologically implausible; developmental trajectories ignored.
Very low-resolution inputs; findings may not hold at realistic scales.
Receptive-field analysis restricted to fovea; eccentricity dependence not examined.
Excluding CLS output token from RF analysis may misrepresent representations actually used.
No control with other training data or objectives; cannot attribute signatures to retinal waves or temporal learning.
Scrambling control confounds temporal order with batch composition and is under-specified.
RF size metric invalid: min-max normalising signed gradients inflates variance.
RF estimated from one stimulus and only centre tokens.
Eq. 6 stride computation gives non-integer value; question.
Edge probe lacks pixel-RDM, Gabor or random baselines and significance tests.
Shape probe may only measure colour invariance from single-channel training.
No seed variability or quantitative effect sizes reported.
Data-size sweep confounds data quantity with number of optimisation steps.
Many hyperparameters missing; no code or checkpoints.
Claim that transformers lack domain priors wrong; patch grid and positional embeddings are priors.
Minor: wrong figure panel reference, 'dissimilarity' misnomer, typo.
Edge emergence expected for many learners; no CNN or sparse-coding baseline discriminates 'learn like brains'.
Shape probe much weaker than neural shape selectivity; satisfied by colour-discarding networks.
Retinotopy never tested; equated with increasing RF sizes.
One-to-one mapping of transformer layers to cortical areas assumed, not shown.
Related work omits sparse coding/ICA, ViT locality, temporal ventral-stream models.
Novelty modest; combination of existing components framed as discovery.
Premise that signatures are present at birth stated as settled though debated.
Simulator-to-image pipeline, frame timing and developmental stage not described.
Genes-unnecessary claim ignores other prenatal signals, molecular cues and designer choices.
No sensitivity analysis to simulator parameters or presets.
Orientation tuning tested at layer level via RDM, not unit-level tuning curves.
RF notion does not map to cortex; no comparison with newborn animal data.
Broader-impact claim of prenatal phase benefit untested; no downstream task.
Non-identifiability: 'learn in common ways' and genes claims untested.
Scrambled control confounds temporal order with batch composition, may break positives.
Probes lack baselines and significance tests.
Shape probe may measure colour invariance.
RF size metric inflated by min-max normalisation of signed gradients.
RF estimated on one stimulus with no occlusion check.
Claim of no domain priors wrong given patch grid and positional embeddings.
Retinotopy equated with RF growth only.
Data-size effect confounded with number of training steps.
Causal verbs used for model-based demonstration.
'Accurate models of brain learning' claim rests on selective citations.
Fig. 2c vs panel (d) reference error.
No results table, effect sizes or seed statistics; only figures and qualitative statements.
Results only for authors' own model/objective without baselines.
Abstract/discussion overclaim: 'same structure', genes unnecessary, accurate models.
Design choices (size, patch, window, presets) unexplained; no ablations.
Results across model sizes only described as 'same pattern'; scaling unreported.
Scrambling protocol only in appendix and ambiguous.
Interpretive causal language mixed into methods/results.
Minor: Fig. 2c/2d reference error, 'dissimilarity' misnomer.

P.summary: Mischaracterisation of Ligeralde et al. in related work.
Temporal-shuffle control cannot isolate spatial vs temporal statistics.
Unsupervised temporal learning method not described.
Self-organization conflated with representational similarity; no topography.
No comparison of model representations with brain data.
Missing control training on non-retinal-wave stimuli.
Incremental novelty relative to Ligeralde et al.
No comparison with prior retinal-wave-trained models.
Long training implausible; developmental trajectory ignored.
CLS token excluded from RF analysis.

Q.summary: No alternative data/objective/learner controls; specificity of retinal waves and temporal learning unshown.
Headline claims (learn like brains, genes unnecessary, accurate models) overreach.
RF size metric flawed by signed-gradient normalisation.
RF estimated from one stimulus and centre tokens only.
Probes lack baselines and significance tests.
Shape probe measures colour invariance, weaker than neural shape selectivity.
No seed statistics, effect sizes or results table.
Data-size sweep confounded with training steps.
Claim that transformers lack spatial priors is wrong.
Layer-area mapping assumed; no comparison with newborn neural data.
Orientation tuning not measured at unit level.
